Title: Infinite loop in rdbLoadObject due to integer promotion mismatch in RDB_TYPE_SET element parsing
Analysis:
The `rdbLoadObject` function in `src/rdb.c` contains an integer promotion mismatch when parsing set objects of type `RDB_TYPE_SET`. Specifically, the set size variable `len` is defined as a `uint64_t`, whereas the loop counter `i` is defined as an `unsigned int` (32-bit).

```c
    uint64_t len;
    unsigned int i;
```

When parsing `RDB_TYPE_SET`, the set size `len` is loaded directly from untrusted input using `rdbLoadLen()`:
```c
    if ((len = rdbLoadLen(rdb,NULL)) == RDB_LENERR) return NULL;
```

The function then iterates over the elements using a `for` loop:
```c
    for (i = 0; i < len; i++) {
```

If a crafted RDB payload is ingested (either through a malicious RDB database file at server boot, replication from a malicious master, or via a `RESTORE` command containing a crafted serialized payload), `len` can be specified as a value greater than `UINT_MAX` (e.g., `4,294,967,296`). Because `i` is a 32-bit unsigned integer, it will increment up to `4,294,967,295` and then wrap back around to `0` instead of reaching `4,294,967,296`. Since `i` is promoted to `uint64_t` for the comparison `i < len`, and `i` can never exceed `UINT_MAX`, the loop condition `i < len` is perpetually true. This causes an infinite loop and hangs the server process, resulting in a severe Denial of Service (DoS).

### Conceptual Exploit Payload (via RESTORE command):
An attacker can send a standard `RESTORE` command with a serialized RDB dump payload:
`RESTORE key 0 "\x0b\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x02\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00..."`
Where the type of the object is set to `RDB_TYPE_SET` (opcode 2), and the variable length field is encoded using `RDB_64BITLEN` to represent a length `>= 2^32` (e.g., `4,294,967,296`). When the server attempts to restore this key, it calls `rdbLoadObject()` which enters the infinite loop and hangs the server process.
